chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): He was asked about a man whose prayer time entered while he was traveling, so he delayed the prayer until he arrived home, intending to pray it when he reached his family, but forgot to pray it upon arrival until the time had passed. He said: 'He prays it two rak'ahs as the prayer of the traveler, because the time entered while he was a traveler, and it was incumbent upon him to pray at that time.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who forgets to pray the shortened prayer until after the time has passed upon returning home?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes that the ruling of a missed prayer is determined by the traveler's status at the onset of its time, not at the moment of performance. Consequently, even if the prayer is missed entirely due to forgetfulness, it retains the 'qasr' (shortened) status of two rak'ahs, reflecting the principle that the legal cause (illah) was present when the obligation attached. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of the traveler's state in determining the form of the prayer.
